facts.text: Sham Shui Po, literally 'Deep Water Pier', earned its name because its waters were deeper than the nearby Cheung Sha Wan beach.
The Lei Cheng Uk Han Tomb, uncovered in 1955, proves Chinese people lived in Sham Shui Po over 2,000 years ago.
Built in 1904, the Sham Shui Po Service Reservoir is Hong Kong's first circular underground water reservoir and a Grade I historic monument.
In 2008, a Sham Shui Po building joined Batch I of the government’s Revitalising Historic Buildings Through Partnership Scheme for adaptive reuse.
The Golden Computer Shopping Arcade in Sham Shui Po is renowned for bargain electronics and accessories.
Originally a coastal settlement on fertile alluvial plains, Sham Shui Po’s shoreline was pushed inland by extensive land reclamation.
